paragraphs.text: Sun and Moon Korean is a Mumbai (Worli) Korean restaurant and kimchi brand selling small-batch fermented kimchi and K-fashion online alongside its dine-in restaurant.

items.title: No educational product content
items.text: Kimchi varieties were listed without explanation, leaving first-time Indian buyers unsure what they were ordering or how it would taste.

items.title: Food and fashion blurred together
items.text: Kimchi and K-fashion products sat in the same undifferentiated catalog, without a clear separation between the two shop experiences.

items.title: No visible trust signals
items.text: Media coverage and customer reviews existed but weren't surfaced on the storefront, leaving an unfamiliar product category without third-party credibility at the point of purchase.

paragraphs.text: Teknoppy's goal was to shape the ecommerce storefront's content, product presentation and shop structure so the site could sell an unfamiliar product category — authentic Korean kimchi — to an Indian audience, while connecting the online store to the restaurant's existing reputation and media coverage.

sections.h2: A comprehensive range of services offered by Teknoppy and their outcomes

items.title: Educational product storytelling
items.text: Each kimchi variety (Baechu, Oi, Pa, Baek, Yeolmu, Mu) carries its Korean name, phonetic English name, and a short flavor/benefit description, helping first-time buyers understand an unfamiliar product before they order.

items.title: Two clear shop categories
items.text: Kimchi and K-fashion are separated into their own shop sections, so the site doesn't blur a food brand with a fashion catalog.

items.title: Trust signals from press and reviews
items.text: Media coverage (Curly Tales, Pinkvilla Hallyutalk) and customer testimonials are surfaced on the homepage, giving an unfamiliar product category third-party credibility.

paragraphs.text: Teknoppy started with the buyer: someone ordering kimchi online for the first time. Each product was explained before it could be bought, the food and fashion catalogues were separated into their own shops, and the restaurant's press coverage and customer reviews were brought onto the storefront so the brand was trusted at the point of purchase.

sections.h2: Sun and Moon Korean's Final Outcome After Teknoppy's Work

items.q: What was the main goal of the Sun and Moon Korean project?
items.a: To help a Mumbai Korean restaurant sell an unfamiliar product — authentic fermented kimchi — online, with a store that educates first-time buyers and builds trust.

items.q: What does Sun and Moon Korean sell online?
items.a: Small-batch fermented kimchi and Korean fashion (K-fashion), from their Worli, Mumbai base.

items.q: Are kimchi and K-fashion sold in the same shop?
items.a: No. Kimchi and K-fashion are separated into their own shop sections, so the site does not blur a food brand with a fashion catalogue.

items.q: How does the store build trust with first-time buyers?
items.a: Every kimchi variety carries its Korean name, phonetic English name and a short flavour and benefit description, and the homepage shows media coverage (Curly Tales, Pinkvilla Hallyutalk) and customer testimonials.
